comment: THE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL EQUALITY MATRIX -- the equality doctrine, as a pinned instrument.
Owner's ruling (repeated; this file exists so it never has to be repeated again):
'breakers, hooks, auditing -- list all the core functionality. outside should ONLY BE
Auth, Store, Protocols, i.e. Plugins. Any plugin gets all functionality.
LLM == MCP == A2A -- just different protocols not different pathway through engine at all.'
Every CORE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL PLANE cell is exactly one of:
proven          -- with `test`: `<repo-relative test file>::<test fn>`. The gate
(crates/busbar/tests/capability_equality.rs) verifies the file exists and
the fn is in it, so a proven cell cannot outlive its evidence.
missing         -- the capability does not reach this plane today, or no test proves it does.
A proof that nobody watched is a claim; MISSING is the honest state until
a named test exists. The missing set is the work queue, and every umbrella
run prints it (scripts/capability-equality-summary.py, wired into
scripts/full-gate.sh) -- green stays green, but the gap is NAMED.
not-applicable  -- with `reason`: a one-line argument. N/A is a claim, not an escape; the
gate refuses an n/a cell whose argument is missing or trivial.
The capability list is the one-of-each modules in core -- each a mechanism that exists
exactly once and that every plane is owed:
breaker.rs, failover/, hooks/, audit/, governance/, metrics.rs, trust/, net_guard.rs,
egress_auth/, catalogue.rs, and the disposition pipeline (proto/ Stage 1 -> breaker::classify).
CHANGING THIS FILE: close a cell by flipping it to `proven` WITH the test that proves it, in
the SAME commit as the test. Regressing a proven cell (its test vanishes or is renamed) is RED.
Adding a capability or plane without filling its whole row/column is RED (the cross product is
exact). Do not delete a capability to shrink the queue.

capabilities.breaker-trip: a failing upstream target records into the ONE core breaker cell (LaneRuntime, (pool,lane)-keyed) and the cell opens
capabilities.breaker-fastfail: a tripped target is refused before dispatch in milliseconds, not after the full timeout, via try_admit_breaker
capabilities.failover-reroute: a second interchangeable candidate is tried before the first byte, through the one selection loop (failover::walk)
capabilities.hooks-tap: observe/transform hooks (rewrite, usage projection) run over the plane's payloads
capabilities.hooks-gate: hooks::gate::decide can refuse the plane's traffic before dispatch
capabilities.audit-chain: the plane's dispatches and refusals land in a tamper-evident hash chain (crate::audit)
capabilities.governance-budget: spend on the plane is attributed to the presenting key and budget limits refuse with a Retry-After
capabilities.disposition: the plane's upstream answers are normalized (Stage 1) and classified into Disposition (Stage 2, breaker::classify)
capabilities.metrics: the plane's traffic appears on the real /metrics scrape under its own plane label
capabilities.trust-pinning: the peer's artifact (schema digest / card fingerprint / SPKI) is pinned; drift is detected, demoted and refused
capabilities.net-guard: every outbound destination this role derives is SSRF-guarded through core net_guard (judged-address pinning, metadata refusal)
capabilities.egress-auth: outbound credentials are planned and injected by the one egress mechanism -- never a caller token passed through
capabilities.catalogue: what this caller may SEE is answered by the one core catalogue walk (catalogue::entitled), trust-gated per item

planes.llm: model traffic: app -> busbar -> provider, HTTP incl. SSE/binary streams (one plane, both halves)
planes.mcp-client: busbar's outbound leg to registered MCP servers -- streamable-HTTP and stdio; where the transport changes the answer, the cell's note says so
planes.mcp-server: busbar's MCP front door: inbound methods from clients and agents
planes.a2a-client: busbar issuing A2A requests: the relay leg to backend agents (JsonRpc, HttpJson, Grpc -- one relay below the transport axis), originate, card fetch
planes.a2a-server: busbar's A2A front door: inbound tasks/messages, plus this role's own outbound webhook push delivery

cells.reason: the front door is inbound; there is no upstream target whose availability could be recorded. A peer-initiated sampling/createMessage rides the LLM engine and is the llm cell's evidence.
inbound role; no upstream availability to record. The anomaly breaker (a2a/anomaly.rs) is behaviour trust, not availability, and must not be conflated with the core breaker.
the front door is inbound; admission-before-dispatch has no upstream target on this role. The outbound legs it triggers are the llm and mcp-client cells.
inbound role; there is no dispatch admission against an upstream to make fast. Refusing inbound work is the governance and trust cells' subject, not the breaker's.
inbound role; there is no candidate set to walk. Failover for work this role triggers belongs to the outbound cells (llm, mcp-client).
inbound role; there is no candidate set to walk on the receiving side. The relay's candidate walk is the a2a-client cell.

cells.note: grep transform under mcp/: zero production hits. The gate projects content to hooks, but there is no observe/transform (rewrite) path over the upstream leg's payloads.
the gate sees content (mcp/tests/hook_gate_tests.rs::mcp_content_reaches_the_gate) but no transform/rewrite path exists for MCP traffic; the tap half of the hook surface is LLM-only today.
no observe/transform hook path over relay/originate payloads; grep transform under a2a/: zero production hits.
the gate sees content (a2a/tests/hook_gate_tests.rs::a2a_content_reaches_the_gate) but there is no transform/rewrite path for inbound A2A payloads.
the gate sits at the method layer (mcp/method.rs) BEFORE the upstream leg; there is no ungated production entry to the client leg, so one battery covers both directions.
originate and push delivery have no hook gate (the '--' row). The relay inherits the inbound gate at receive.rs, but busbar-originated A2A traffic is ungated.

grep crate::audit under proxy/: zero production hits. Model requests have billing/telemetry but land in NO tamper-evident chain; MCP (calllog) and A2A (provenance) both do. This is the doctrine inverted -- the flagship plane is the unproven one.

the front-door call record covers relayed tools/call transactions (mcp-server cell), and upstream.rs uses audit vocab words for refusals, but no test proves a client-leg outcome lands in a chain of its own.
task provenance chains inbound task events (a2a-server cell); no test proves originate or push-delivery outcomes are chained.
the transaction is charged at the front door (mcp-server cell); no test proves the upstream leg's spend is separately attributed or limited when busbar itself originates the leg.

cells.reason: disposition classifies an upstream's ANSWER; the inbound role has no upstream answer to classify. Rendering a refusal to a caller is the response path, not disposition.
disposition classifies an upstream's ANSWER; the inbound role has no upstream answer to classify. Rendering a refusal to a caller is the response path, not disposition.

cells.note: despite its name the test drives all three planes and asserts the llm, mcp and a2a series labels on one real scrape.
the plane-label series is driven by inbound traffic; no test proves a client-leg-specific series (upstream latency, per-server outcome) exists.
the plane-label series is driven by inbound traffic; no test proves a relay/originate-leg series (backend latency, per-agent outcome) exists.

cells.reason: LLM providers are operator-declared config endpoints, not peer-published artifacts; there is no upstream-authored schema or card to pin. The trust lifecycle governs artifacts a peer authors.

LLM egress targets are operator-configured provider endpoints; no request-authored URL reaches the LLM egress path, so there is no SSRF surface -- which is why grep finds no net_guard consumer under proxy/.
the inbound listener derives no outbound destination of its own; the destinations its work triggers are guarded in the mcp-client and llm cells.

cells.note: this role's own outbound is webhook push delivery, and it is guarded -- the PUSH-DELIVER TCK waivers exist because this guard correctly wins over the conformance score.

cells.reason: this role's only outbound (peer sampling) rides the LLM engine, whose credential injection is the llm cell; inbound caller authentication is the Auth plugin's subject, not egress.
